title: Playing in difficult keys without lessons; arrival in 1910
summary: He says he had only five or six lessons, learned by ear, kept returning to New Orleans, and first arrived there in 1910.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And I worked, I worked, I played for her at the Dauphine Theater, and I forgot the name of the piano player. He was violin there for years, he was playing the show. So he sat out there and watched me, cause she was singing, instead of easy keys, instead of F, it'd be four sharps. Instead of being flat, it'd be five sharps. And I can, listen, I only had five lessons. I worked with Johnny Krueger at the, at the Colleton Sisters for eight months, and I was going crazy cause I'd take some of the heavy stuff. I, I used to, I don't know, my mother was a fine pianist, my father, like I told her, sang her. They sang the Academy of Music in New York and all that.
Yeah. I couldn't take any lessons.

I couldn't take any lessons. I'm pretty sure I didn't have no more than five or six. But I could go out and pick up Rosier Grady, take East Side, West Side, from a little number that taught me from the company. And I finally jumped around the piano and went down the bass and later on I found augments and diminishes and all that kind of stuff. It come to me natural. See? Well I go back to Mila Coma again, twice. I couldn't stay away with rice and beans and good gumbo and good fine oysters that fifteen cents a dozen, two dozen for a quarter, a big glass of beer, you know, for nickel. Well we never had those things up in New York. I'm born in Louisville, Kentucky, see. My father took us all as kids to New York, my mother, and they went and sing an opera, so. But anyway that's how I got to New Orleans. I took freight trains and what they call side dog Pullmans. Yeah. What year did you get here?
What year did you get here first? 1910.

1910. That's seventy years ago. I'll be ninety next April. And this is what's kept me alive, I tell everybody drink beer. Well New York's at Egan telling me when we worked at the nightclub, I used to drink six and seven. Just cause the people bought them.
